stop.ramp_duration_s.basis: Operator decision: Operator-approved 2026-10-24 after D9 trial 1: the 0.2 s stop ramp kept the last impedance torque and the arm accelerated (joint 6 to 1.64 rad/s, TCP 11.4 cm during the stop); ramp 0.01 s and stronger big-joint damping from fitted effective inertias (decay ~0.05 s); measured-speed guard relaxed from 20% to ~45% of the Panda limits; wrist command-torque guard 8 -> 12 N m (FR3 rated wrist torque): the first-row target step of normal DROID chunks requests transient raw impedance torque up to 8.5 N m on the wrist (76 D7 chunks, 8 would trip at 8 N m) and 9.9 N m in D9 episode 2; the sent torque is rate-limited to 1 N m per ms; after D9 episode 2 retry (TCP 7.1 cm during stop, joint 2 decay 0.21 s): big-joint stop damping (15,20,15,5) from fitted effective inertias (0.68, 1.04, 0.66 kg m^2) for ~0.05 s decay; operator asked to relax the measured-speed guard further: 1.5 / 1.8 rad/s (~70% of the Panda limits), damping torque at guard speed <= 30 N m; operator chose torque admission (option A) after D9 episode 3 (0.2 rad wrist reversal requested 18.4 N m): reject chunks whose predicted reference-step torque exceeds 0.9 x the command-torque guard (fraction proposed by the engineer); hold after a rejected chunk 200 -> 1000 ms (operator decision after D9 episode 5: consecutive rejections at ~75 ms intervals expired the 200 ms hold; the arm holds its last target under impedance meanwhile)
